rule: Michigan's state races on the November 3, 2026 ballot, keyed by the race ids in ballot_local_2026.sqlite, by the same rule as the Congress pages (ballot/polls/polls_2026.json) and Minnesota's file (polls_mn_state_2026.json). Polls only from pollsters in AAPOR's Transparency Initiative (John, 2026-09-29): the latest from up to five of them, and our own average of the ten most recent, the arithmetic shown. Each poll's figures are checked against the pollster's own release; a list of polls (Wikipedia's, labelled as secondary) is used only to find them and to count the polls left out.

polls.note: The question named the two candidates for governor, not their running mates, and offered "another party's candidate" without naming the Libertarian, Green or U.S. Taxpayers tickets. The table packet gives another party's candidate 2%, undecided 4% and no response under 1%.
The release names the two candidates for governor, not their running mates, and gives 6% undecided; it does not say what the remaining 3% answered.

The question named Jocelyn Benson, the Democrat, and John James, the Republican, without running mates or the other three tickets; the figures include people who said which way they lean. Neither 5%, other 4%, no opinion under half a percent. SSRS interviewed 843 registered voters and reports likely voters by weighting each by a predicted probability of voting; the margin given is for those results.

polls.pollster: Michigan State University (IPPSR, fielded by YouGov)
polls.member: Institute for Public Policy and Social Research, and the Office for Survey Research, at Michigan State University
polls.sample: 779 likely voters; the release states no margin of error
polls.note: The State of the State Survey: 1,000 Michigan adults from a YouGov online panel, of whom 913 were registered voters and 779 likely voters. Among registered voters the release gives Benson 49% and James 39%. It states no margin of error (Wikipedia's list gives 3.4 points; the release does not), and does not say what the rest answered.

Mitchell Research (twelve: two of November's matchup, three with Mike Duggan, three of the Democratic primary and four of the Republican)
Rosetta Stone Communications (three, from one survey of October 2025)

left_out.note: The count is of separate rows as Wikipedia lists them, by pollsters outside the Transparency Initiative: 17 of Benson against James, 13 of Benson, James and Mike Duggan (the former mayor of Detroit ran as an independent and withdrew; he is not on the ballot), 9 of the Democratic primary and 23 of the Republican primary. Questions with other possible nominees came from the same surveys and are not counted again. Wikipedia lists 23 polls of Benson against James in all: the four shown here, the two pending and the 17 left out. AARP belongs to the Transparency Initiative but its Michigan poll was taken by Fabrizio Ward and Impact Research, which do not. Three more surveys by members are not shown because they did not ask November's two-way matchup: Michigan State University's of March 2-24, 2026 (1,000 adults) asked Benson, James and Duggan together, and Emerson's of April 11-13 and July 26-27, 2026 asked only the primaries; Emerson's January 2026 Michigan survey did not ask about the governor's race. Emerson's site lists no Michigan release after September 17 (read 2026-10-02). The same four surveys are in the Congress file for Michigan's Senate race.
